extracted.intended_audience: applicants, practitioners, and draftsmen preparing and filing U.S. design patent applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and legal/regulatory standards for preparing, drawing, and prosecuting design patent applications in the United States, including required content, drawing standards, oath/declaration and application data sheet rules, and applicable statutes and CFR rules. Intended to govern how to produce acceptable filings and how examination/reconsideration proceeds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of address notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Notification of “Change of Address” should be made by separate letter, and a separate notification should be filed for each application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File change-of-address notifications as separate letters for each application to ensure proper recognition by the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration after reply to Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon submission of a reply to an Office action, the application will be reconsidered and further examined in view of applicant's remarks and any amendments included with the reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner will withdraw rejection and allow the application if persuaded, or repeat the rejection and make it Final if not. Applicant may file an appeal after a final rejection or after the claim has been rejected twice, or file a new application claiming benefit of the earlier filing date prior to abandonment to continue prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shading types for design drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Two types of shading commonly employed in design patent application drawings are straight-line surface shading and stippling; individually or in combination they can effectively represent the character and contour of most surfaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use straight-line surface shading or stippling (or both on different surfaces) to represent surface character and contour. Do not use stippling and straight-line surface shading together on the same surface.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on mixing shading on same surface
rubrics_metrics.description: Both stippling and straight-line surface shading, while permissible on the same object to show surface contrast, should not be used together on the same surface.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If showing surface contrast on an object, apply different shading techniques to different surfaces but avoid applying multiple shading techniques to a single surface to prevent confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depicting transparent materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Elements visible behind transparent surfaces should be shown in light, full lines, not broken lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When illustrating transparent materials (e.g., aquarium, perfume bottle), show behind-the-surface elements with light solid lines so they are visible but not claimed as separate elements via broken lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broken-line disclosure (environmental/boundary features)
rubrics_metrics.description: Broken lines may be used to show environment and boundaries that form no part of the claimed design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use broken lines to indicate surrounding environment or boundary elements that are not claimed; these should not be interpreted as claim elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploded view rules
rubrics_metrics.description: An exploded view is only supplementary to a fully assembled view. A bracket must be employed to show the association of elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a fully assembled view as primary; use exploded views only as supplements and show separation association with brackets (e.g., set of game components example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate positions must be separate views
rubrics_metrics.description: The alternate positions of a design, or an element of the design, must be shown in separate views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not attempt to show alternate positions superimposed in a single view (unless broken line superimposition is acceptable without crowding); provide distinct views for alternate positions to avoid ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indeterminate length indication
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of a separation and a bracket to indicate that, for ease of illustration, the precise length of the molding is not claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a part's exact length is not claimed, indicate indeterminate length by showing separation and a bracket to avoid inadvertently claiming a specific length (e.g., picture frame molding).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of cross-sectional views
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-sections may be employed to clarify the disclosure and to minimize the number of views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include sectional views where necessary; indicate the cutting plane (broken line with numerals and arrows) and use appropriate hatching to show materials and avoid obscuring reference characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple embodiments in one design application
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple embodiments of a single concept may be filed in one design application, so long as their appearance and shape are similar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may include related embodiments in one application to economize filings, provided the embodiments are similar in overall appearance and shape; use views to clearly distinguish embodiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depicting specific materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings may depict specific materials or ornamental effects when material is relevant to the appearance of the design (e.g., sandal, multi-pocketed storage bag examples).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If material or texture/ornamental effect is part of the claimed appearance, depict it clearly in the drawings (via shading, stippling, notes, or appropriate views).

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphical symbols for draftsmen
rubrics_metrics.description: Graphical symbols for conventional elements may be used on the drawing when appropriate, subject to approval by the Office. Other standard and commonly used symbols will also be acceptable provided they are clearly understood, adequately identified in the specification as filed, and do not create confusion with other symbols used in patent drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you use symbols, identify them in the specification; in lieu of a symbol you may show a conventional element by an appropriately labeled rectangle, square or circle; avoid ambiguous abbreviations unless their meaning is evident and not confusing.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 102 — Conditions for patentability; novelty and loss of right to patent
rubrics_metrics.description: A person shall be entitled to a patent unless the invention was known or used by others, patented or described in a printed publication, in public use, on sale, abandoned, previously patented abroad, or otherwise disclosed more than applicable time limits before the applicant's invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meet the novelty requirements: check prior patents, printed publications, public use, sale, abandonment, foreign filings and published applications. Note special timing rules (e.g., one-year grace periods and publication-by-others exceptions) and the statutory enumerated subsections (a)-(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 103 — Conditions for patentability; non-obvious subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent may not be obtained if the differences between the subject matter sought to be patented and the prior art are such that the subject matter as a whole would have been obvious to a person having ordinary skill in the art at the time the invention was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess obviousness against the ordinary skill person standard; note special biotechnology provisions (timely election to proceed under subsection for certain biotech processes and compositions) and ownership/assignment considerations affecting prior-art treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 112 — Specification requirements (written description, enablement, best mode)
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification shall contain a written description of the invention, and the manner and process of making and using it, in full, clear, concise, and exact terms to enable a person skilled in the art to make and use the invention, and shall set forth the best mode contemplated by the inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the specification provides sufficient written description and enablement, and disclose the best mode. Avoid adding new matter in later amendments. Claims must particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter regarded as the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim form rules under 35 U.S.C. 112
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim may be written in independent or, if the nature of the case admits, in dependent or multiple dependent form. Dependent claims must refer to a previous claim and specify a further limitation; multiple dependent claims reference alternatives and incorporate limitations by reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft claims in appropriate dependent/independent forms; multiple dependent claims cannot serve as basis for other multiple dependent claims; understand incorporation-by-reference effects for claim construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Means-plus-function claim provision (35 U.S.C. 112 paragraph)
rubrics_metrics.description: An element in a claim for a combination may be expressed as a means or step for performing a specified function without recital of structure, material, or acts, and such claim shall be construed to cover the corresponding structure, material, or acts described in the specification and equivalents thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using means/step language, ensure the specification discloses corresponding structure/material/acts sufficiently to support the means-plus-function claim; otherwise the claim may be limited or invalid.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 132 — Notice of rejection and reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever, on examination, any claim is rejected, the Director shall notify the applicant stating the reasons with useful information and references. If applicant persists in the claim, the application shall be reexamined. No amendment shall introduce new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear reasons in Office actions; applicants must avoid introducing new matter in amendments; the Director may set regulations for continued examination and fees with small-entity reductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 171 — Patents for designs
rubrics_metrics.description: Whoever invents any new, original, and ornamental design for an article of manufacture may obtain a patent therefor, subject to the conditions and requirements of this title. Provisions relating to patents for inventions apply to design patents except as provided otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design patents cover new, original, ornamental designs. Follow general patent laws unless specific exceptions for designs apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 172 — Right of priority for designs
rubrics_metrics.description: The right of priority provided by sections 119(a)-(d) and the time specified in section 102(d) shall be six months in the case of designs. The right of priority under section 119(e) does not apply to designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When claiming priority to earlier foreign filings for designs, comply with the six-month priority period; do not rely on 119(e) (provisional) for designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 173 — Term of design patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents for designs shall be granted for the term of fourteen years from the date of grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect a 14-year enforceable term from grant for design patents (statutory term at time of this guide).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.3 — Conduct with decorum and courtesy
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants and their attorneys or agents are required to conduct their business with the Patent and Trademark Office with decorum and courtesy. Papers presented in violation will be submitted to the Commissioner and returned by direct order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid improper language or filings; submit complaints against examiners or employees in separate correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.63 — Oath or declaration general requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An oath or declaration filed as part of a nonprovisional application must be executed (signed) properly; identify each inventor by full name (family name and at least one given name), identify country of citizenship, and state belief that the named inventor(s) are the original and first inventors of the claimed subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the oath/declaration is competently signed, names are fully given (no abbreviations for primary given name), and contains the inventor-citizenship and originality statements required by statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.63 — Oath or declaration additional content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to general requirements, the oath/declaration must identify the application to which it is directed; state that the signer has reviewed and understands the contents of the application including claims as amended; and acknowledge the duty to disclose all information known to be material to patentability (§1.56).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include explicit statements in the oath/declaration attesting to review of the application and acknowledgment of duty of disclosure; failure to acknowledge can have prosecution consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.63 — Inventor contact and foreign application details in oath/declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless supplied on an application data sheet, the oath or declaration must also identify mailing address (and residence if different) of each inventor, and any foreign application for which priority is claimed by specifying application number, country, and filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Either include this bibliographic information in the oath/declaration or supply it on an ADS; be precise about foreign priority details to support priority claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.63 — Continuation/divisional/continuation-in-part rules for oaths/declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: A newly executed oath/declaration is not required in a continuation or divisional if the prior application contained the required oath/declaration and certain conditions are met (same inventors or fewer, no new matter, copy of executed oath submitted, statements for deletions, etc.). Newly executed oaths are required in some cases (e.g., naming a new inventor) and continuation-in-part applications always require a new oath/declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specified conditions and submit required copies/statements when relying on prior oaths for continuation/divisional filings; file new oaths when necessary (e.g., new inventors or CIPs).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.76 — Application data sheet (ADS) and required bibliographic data
rubrics_metrics.description: An application data sheet is a sheet or sheets that may be voluntarily submitted containing bibliographic data in an Office-specified format; if provided, the ADS is part of the application. Bibliographic data includes applicant information, correspondence information, application information (title, suggested classification, number of drawing sheets, application type, etc.), representative information, domestic priority, foreign priority, and assignee information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing information via an ADS can satisfy statutory references (e.g., 35 U.S.C. 119(e)/120) and eases bibliographic capture. Ensure ADS fields are complete and accurate (names, addresses, application type, priority data, representative registration numbers, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.76 — Supplemental ADS and changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplemental application data sheets may be supplied prior to payment of the issue fee to correct or update information in a previously submitted ADS or oath/declaration, except that inventorship, correspondence, and citizenship changes are governed by other rules; supplemental ADS should identify only the changed information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use supplemental ADS to update data before issue fee; do not rely on ADS to effect changes governed by other sections (e.g., inventorship §1.48). Identify specific changes to avoid re-submitting unchanged data.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.76 — Inconsistencies between ADS and oath/declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: For inconsistencies between information supplied by an ADS and by an oath/declaration, the latest submitted information will govern; if supplied at the same time the ADS governs except that the oath/declaration governs inconsistencies in naming of inventors and citizenship. The Office initially captures bibliographic information from the ADS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When ADS and oath conflict, know which document controls; be careful when submitting both and understand that the Office will generally rely on ADS-captured bibliographic data and recapture only upon request and fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.84(a) — Acceptable drawing media: black ink and color drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Black and white drawings are normally required; India ink or equivalent must secure solid black lines. Color drawings are permitted only on rare occasions when necessary to disclose the subject matter, must be reproducible in black & white, are not permitted in international applications or EFS-Web submissions, and require a petition with fee and supporting material (three sets of color drawings, a B/W photocopy, and a specification amendment noting color drawings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use black ink drawings by default. If color is essential, file a petition with required sets, fee, and amending language; expect stricter scrutiny and additional requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.84(b) — Photographs in applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographs (including photocopies) are not ordinarily permitted but will be accepted if photographs are the only practicable medium for illustrating the claimed invention (examples include gels, blots, cell cultures, histological tissue sections, animals, plants, in vivo imaging, thin layer structures, and ornamental effects in design applications). Photographs must be of sufficient quality for reproducibility in the printed patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only use photographs when drawings cannot practically depict the subject matter. Be prepared to replace photographs with drawings if the examiner requires it and ensure photographs meet high-quality reproduction standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.84(c)-(d) — Identification and graphic forms in drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Identifying indicia (title, inventor's name, application or docket number) if provided should be centered within the top margin of each sheet. Chemical/mathematical formulae, tables, and waveforms may be submitted as drawings and are subject to the same requirements; label separate formulae as separate figures and present groups of waveforms with a common vertical axis and individual waveform identifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place identifying information properly on drawing sheets; when submitting scientific graphics, follow figure labeling and integration conventions so the Office treats them as drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.84(e)-(g) — Paper type, size, and margins for drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings must be on flexible, strong, white, smooth, non-shiny durable paper, reasonably free from cracks/creases/erasures; only one side of sheet used. All drawing sheets in an application must be the same size (A4 or 8.5x11 inches). Margins: top ≥2.5 cm (1”), left ≥2.5 cm (1”), right ≥1.5 cm (5/8”), bottom ≥1.0 cm (3/8”), leaving specified sight area limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere strictly to paper quality, uniform sheet size, and margin dimensions to avoid rejection or nonconforming drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.84(h)-(i) — Views requirements and arrangement
rubrics_metrics.description: The drawing must contain as many views as necessary to show the invention (plan, elevation, section, perspective). Views must be grouped together, arranged without wasting space, upright, clearly separated, not included with specification pages, not connected by projection lines, and must not contain centerlines. Exploded views must use brackets; partial views must be linkable edge-to-edge and include a smaller-scale whole view; sectional views must indicate the cutting plane and use appropriate hatching; very long views may be divided clearly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide adequate views to fully disclose appearance; follow specific conventions for exploded, partial, sectional, and very long views. Use labels and numbering to indicate sectional planes and ensure hatching and linework do not obscure reference characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.84(h)(4)-(5) and (j) — Alternate/modified positions and front-page view
rubrics_metrics.description: A moved (alternate) position may be shown by a broken line superimposed on a suitable view if not crowded; otherwise use a separate view. Modified forms of construction must be shown in separate views. One view should be suitable for inclusion on the front page of the patent application publication and patent; applicant may suggest a single view by figure number for front page inclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid crowding when showing alternate positions; choose a clear front-page figure for publication and suggest it to the Office. Provide separate views when necessary to show modifications or alternate positions unambiguously.
